rules.description: A part must exist in the catalogue and be VERIFIED and orderable before it can be ordered.
Some parts need the machine variant identified before the right part is certain.

provenance.reference: IdentificationRequirement nodes are shown in part views but are not enforced at checkout

rules.description: When a machine is selected, a part that is not recorded as fitting that machine is refused.
Requester and receiver need a name, a valid email and phone, and the destination must be a recorded ship-to.
If dealer installation is requested, the chosen dealer must be recorded as installing every ordered part.
A depot can supply the order only if every line has known stock of at least the quantity and a recorded route reaches the destination. Unknown stock is never treated as zero.
A repeated place-order with the same key returns the existing order; nothing new is created.
Order totals are not calculated; the freight figure is a synthetic estimate shown as context only.
Allocation reserves every line or none, in one transaction with row locks.
Two orders cannot reserve the same units.
From ALLOCATION_FAILED the processor can retry allocation, reject the order or cancel it.
Each order action is valid only from specific statuses and is checked on the server.
A dispatched shipment is delivered, reports an exception (which can be resumed), or fails delivery.

provenance.reference: app/services/order_flow.py ACTIONS deliver, shipment_exception, resume_shipment, delivery_failed

rules.description: Tracking events must start with ORDER_CONFIRMED or PICKED, follow the allowed transitions, and carry a location unless IN_TRANSIT.
An order with dealer service completes when the service completes; without service it completes after delivery.
A claim is evaluated deterministically against fitment, approved part, authorised dealer, coverage window, installation evidence, and prior claims or replacements.
A reviewer accepts or declines a claim marked REQUIRES_REVIEW. No review step is implemented.
